2026-10-22.note: Free evening, nothing on for tea

steps: Cook the pasta according to the pack instructions, then drain and run under cold water to cool slightly.
Cook the sweetcorn for 3–4 minutes if frozen, or just drain if tinned.
Mix the tuna, mayonnaise and lemon juice in a big bowl.
Stir in the pasta, sweetcorn and red pepper. Season.
Serve with salad leaves on the side.
recipe.tip: Mathilda: keep her tuna mayo light, and swap the raw pepper for cucumber sticks on the side if she's not keen.

2026-10-23.meal: Air-fryer veggie sausages with crispy potato wedges & beans
2026-10-23.note: Normal evening — gymnastics & swimming earlier today, nothing on for tea

ingredients: 1/2 tsp smoked paprika (for the grown-ups' wedges)
steps: Toss the potato wedges in the oil, season, and air fry at 200°C for 12 minutes.
Add the paprika to the wedges for the grown-ups now, keeping Mathilda and Francis's plain.
Add the veggie sausages to the air fryer basket alongside the wedges and cook for a further 8-10 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and the wedges are crisp.
Heat the beans in a small pan or the microwave for 3-4 minutes.
Serve the sausages and wedges with the beans.
recipe.tip: Mathilda: cut her sausage into coins and keep her wedges plain.

2026-10-24.note: This week's one meat night. Francis at the nerd convention, Jess & Mathilda seeing cousins today — slow cooker on before you head out so tea's ready whenever everyone's back

ingredients: 1 tbsp cornflour, mixed with a splash of water
Crusty bread or mash, to serve
steps: Put the onion, carrots, celery and leeks into the slow cooker.
Add the chicken thighs on top, then the tomatoes, stock, tomato purée and thyme. Season.
Cover and cook on low for 6-7 hours (or high for 3-4) until the chicken is tender and falling apart.
About 20 minutes before serving, stir in the cornflour slurry to thicken, and shred the chicken through the sauce.
Serve with crusty bread or mash.
recipe.tip: On by 8-9am before you head out. Mathilda: mash her portion with a fork and check for bones. Freeze any leftovers fully cooled, portioned and labelled for the meal drawer.

2026-10-25.note: Free day — good one for batch cooking. Make extra to reheat on Tuesday after Hull hockey training

ingredients: 1 veg stock cube, dissolved in 600ml hot water
Parmesan or vegetarian hard cheese, to serve
steps: Soften the onions, garlic, carrots and celery in the oil in a large pan for 8 minutes.
Add the rinsed lentils, passata, tomato purée, herbs and stock. Stir well and season.
Simmer gently for 25-30 minutes, stirring now and then, until the lentils are soft and the sauce is thick. Add a splash of water if it gets too thick.
Take out Mathilda's portion and 4 portions to cool for Tuesday before adding any extra pepper or chilli to the rest.
About 15 minutes before tea, cook the spaghetti for 10 minutes and drain.
Serve the sauce over the spaghetti with grated cheese.
Cool Tuesday's 4 portions within an hour, then cover and keep in the fridge (no need to freeze).
recipe.tip: Mathilda: mash her lentils a little finer if she's fussy about texture.

2026-10-26.note: Half term starts today — evening's free, nothing on for tea

steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Boil the new potatoes for 15 minutes until tender.
Put the salmon skin-side down on a lined tray. Drizzle with oil, squeeze over half the lemon and season.
Bake for 12-15 minutes, until it flakes easily.
Steam or boil the green beans for the last 4 minutes of the potatoes.
Drain the potatoes and toss with the butter. Serve with lemon wedges.
recipe.tip: Air fryer instead: 180°C for 10-12 minutes. Flake Mathilda's portion and check carefully for bones.

2026-10-27.meal: Reheat: Sunday's lentil bolognese with spaghetti
2026-10-27.note: Hull hockey training 6-7pm (Hymers College) plus travel — tea ready for whoever's not driving, kept warm for the rest

ingredients: 4 portions of Sunday's lentil bolognese sauce (from the fridge)
Parmesan or vegetarian hard cheese, to serve
steps: Tip the bolognese into a pan with a splash of water and heat gently, stirring, until bubbling and piping hot all the way through (about 8-10 minutes). Or microwave in a covered bowl for 4-5 minutes, stirring halfway.
Cook the spaghetti for 10 minutes while the sauce heats, then drain.
Serve with grated cheese. Anyone back late from training can have their portion microwaved separately.
recipe.tip: Only reheat it once, and check it's piping hot all the way through before serving.

2026-10-28.meal: Baked cod with lemon & herb crumb, new potatoes & green beans
2026-10-28.note: Hockey Academy Night 6:15-7:45pm (The Lindum) — air fryer gets tea done fast either side of the run

ingredients: Small handful fresh parsley, chopped (or 1 tsp dried)
steps: Boil the new potatoes for 15 minutes until tender.
Mix the breadcrumbs, lemon zest, parsley, melted butter and a pinch of salt.
Put the cod fillets in the air fryer basket and press the crumb on top.
Air fry at 180°C for 10-12 minutes, until the crumb is golden and the fish flakes.
Cook the beans for the last 4 minutes of the potatoes. Serve with lemon wedges.
recipe.tip: Mathilda: leave the lemon zest off her portion and check carefully for bones.

2026-10-29.meal: Jacket potatoes, tuna mayo or cheese & beans
2026-10-29.note: Mathilda's hospital eye test is at 2:20pm (dilating drops — she may be unsettled after) — keeping tea simple and familiar tonight

steps: Prick the potatoes all over and microwave on high for 10 minutes to soften.
Transfer to the air fryer at 200°C for 20-25 minutes, until the skins are crisp. (Or straight in the oven at 200°C/180°C fan for 60-75 minutes if you'd rather skip the microwave.)
Mix the tuna with the mayonnaise.
Heat the beans in a pan or the microwave for 3-4 minutes.
Split the potatoes open and top with tuna mayo, cheese or beans.
Serve with salad leaves if anyone wants them.
recipe.tip: Mathilda: she may be sensitive to light and a bit out of sorts after today's eye drops — give her cheese and beans rather than tuna if she's not keen, and keep the lights low for tea.
